title: Economic-aware rollback manager for config changes with staged throttles
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an automated rollback manager that evaluates the economic and reliability impact of config changes (batching, cache TTLs, kernel selection) and performs safe, incremental reverts when a change degrades golden signals or increases inferred unit cost beyond a configurable tolerance.

Approach overview: build a controller that sits between config_apply and the runtime rollout engine. When a config change is staged, the controller attaches a short-lived orchestration lease (safety token), provisions a staged canary cohort, and applies incremental throttles: progressive shard percentage, max QPS cap, and batching window limits. The controller continuously evaluates a compact policy that blends SLO delta (error rate, p95/p99 latency), cache evictions/hit-rate, and inferred cost-per-1000-tokens. If the combined score exceeds thresholds, the manager triggers automated rollback actions with graded severity: slow-down & reconfigure -> partial revert -> full revert.

Key algorithms and state: 
- Economic score = weighted sum of: relative cost delta, tail-latency penalty, and request-failure rate. Weights are tenant-configurable with sane defaults (cost=0.4, latency=0.4, errors=0.2).
- Hysteresis windows: require N consecutive evaluation windows (configurable, default 3) before escalating to a revert to avoid noisy flips.
- Idempotent reconciliation: controller stores applied-change fingerprint and target-state in the control-plane DB; reconciliation loop is idempotent and tolerates partial apply failures. Every change records a compaction record to be used by the revert path to reconstruct prior state exactly (including batching params and cache TTLs).
- Safe-apply semantics: all config changes are applied behind a two-phase apply: Preflight validation -> Staged apply (cohort) -> Promote. Reverts can operate at any phase and support out-of-band emergency revert.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but increase blast radius time; we default to conservative and provide a fast opt-in aggressive profile for non-production namespaces.
- Full transactional rollback across heterogeneous deployments (hosted/dedicated/private) is complex; we implement best-effort multi-phase compensating actions and record audit logs for manual reconciliation in Private deployments.

Expected integrations: rollout engine, tracing/metrics pipeline, cost analytics job, Console for operator overrides, and audit logging/KMS for signed apply tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Controller applies staged cohort changes and advances promotion after stable windows
Economic score computed in realtime from metrics (cost delta, p95, error-rate) and exposed in Console
Automated rollback triggers at configurable thresholds with three severity levels and produces signed revert operations
Reconciliation loop is idempotent: repeated runs converge to target state within 60s under flaky network
End-to-end e2e test covering staged apply -> growth -> regression -> automated rollback passes in CI
tasks: Design spec: cost-aware rollback state machine (doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/cost-rollback-spec)
Proto: lightweight controller skeleton + reconciliation loop (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8123)
Metrics plumbing: add derived cost-per-1k-tokens and expose as metric 'inference.econ.cost_per_1k'
Console: add UI for thresholds, override, and rollback audit trail (mockup: https://drive.google.com/mockup/rollback-ui)
Integrations: wire controller to rollout engine and dedicated VPC agent via signed apply-token flow
CI: add e2e harness that simulates increased latency and verifies rollback path
comments: 2025-01-12 - Asha Patel: Drafted spec and initial score function. Shared with runtime and console for feedback.
2025-01-18 - Marcus King (runtime): Recommended adding KV-cache eviction metric as an input; updated scoring to include cache_hit_rate delta.
2025-01-25 - Priya Nair (SRE): Raised concern about rollback frequency during flash cold-start traffic; suggested adaptive hysteresis tied to request volume.
2025-02-02 - Luis Romero: Implemented controller skeleton and reconciliation loop. Submitted PR for initial review (link in tasks).
2025-02-10 - Design review: UX team requested a compact audit view showing pre/post economic delta for each automated revert. Adding to Console task list.
2025-02-14 - QA: e2e failure observed where partial revert on private deployments left stale feature flags; added compensating cleanup step to revert path.
risk_mitigation: Limit automated rollbacks to non-production by default; require operator approval for private deployments via signed apply-token. Implement multi-window hysteresis and noise-tolerant scoring. Maintain full audit trail and an emergency manual revert API. Add feature-flagged aggressive mode for experiments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal runtime namespaces only, conservative thresholds, observe for 2 weeks. Phase 2: opt-in tenant beta with console override and increased telemetry retention. Phase 3: enable auto-rollback for low-risk namespaces by default and document operator runbooks.
notes: We should coordinate with legal for audit retention policy for Private deployments.
Consider adding model-quality signal (e.g., eval-set regressions) once eval infra exposes a realtime metric.
Follow-on: expose a simulation mode that replays historical telemetry against candidate configs to estimate economic impact before apply.
